legend: Monke likes mind-boggling functions that even a genius like him can't solve. The function is the following —
f(k,x)=∑y&x=yf(k−1,y)%%ZSMJ1%%, in other words, summation of f(k−1,y)%%ZSMJ2%% for all y%%ZSMJ3%% that are submask of x%%ZSMJ4%%, i.e. (y&x=y)%%ZSMJ5%%.

Monke tried to write a code that finds f(k,x)%%ZSMJ6%% mod%%ZSMJ7%% 109+7%%ZSMJ8%%. When he runs that code, his computer catches on fire, he loses his mind and comes to you. Now, to calm him down (and to also prove you're more of a genius than him), you have to write a code that can calculate f(k,x)%%ZSMJ9%% modulo%%ZSMJ10%% 109+7%%ZSMJ11%%, which doesn't burn Monke's computer.
input: The first line of input contains t(1≤t≤105)%%ZSMJ12%% — the number of test cases.
Each test case contains two integers k,x(1≤k,x≤3⋅105)%%ZSMJ13%%.
